title: How do batteries work?
examples: Teacher, what is the difference between a battery and a generator?
If I use up all the power, can I make the battery work again?
Does the type of chemicals affect how much power it gives?

explain.say: A battery stores energy in a chemical form.
The chemical reaction inside creates a flow of electrons.

items: Electrons flowing from negative to positive

explain.say: Batteries have two ends called terminals for connecting.
Some batteries can be recharged by supplying electricity.
A simple example is using a dry cell in a torch.
In a car, the chemical energy is used to move the wheels.

faq.q: What is the difference between a battery and a generator?
faq.a: A battery stores chemical energy that is converted to electricity. A generator usually uses mechanical energy, like spinning, to create electricity.
asks: How are batteries different from generators?
Do batteries make electricity from movement?

faq.q: Can I use a battery if the terminals are not connected?
faq.a: No, electricity needs a complete circuit to flow. The terminals must connect a path to the load, like a bulb.
asks: Does the circuit need to be closed?
What happens if I break the connection?

faq.q: What does it mean when a battery is 'fully discharged'?
faq.a: It means the chemical reactants inside have mostly been used up. There are not enough chemicals left to create a strong electrical current.
asks: What does 'discharged' mean for a battery?

faq.q: Why do some batteries need to be recharged?
faq.a: Rechargeable batteries can be chemically reset by applying an external electric current. This reverses the chemical reaction that happened during use.
asks: How do I make a battery work again?
Is it always possible to recharge a battery?

faq.q: Are all batteries made of the same chemicals?
faq.a: No, different devices use different types of chemicals. For example, alkaline batteries use different chemicals than lithium batteries.
asks: Does the chemical matter for the battery?

facts: Batteries convert stored chemical energy into electrical energy.
The terminals are the positive and negative ends of the battery.
A complete circuit is necessary for electricity to flow from the battery.
Recharging forces an external current to restore the chemicals.

quiz.say: If a battery is used, what type of energy is primarily being used up?
quiz.why: The battery stores energy chemically, so using it consumes the chemicals.

wrong.1: This is the energy that comes out, not the energy that is stored inside.
wrong.2: Heat is a byproduct, but it is not the main form of energy stored.
wrong.3: This energy relates to motion, which is not the stored form.

quiz.say: Which part of the battery is usually marked with a plus sign?
quiz.why: The positive terminal is the designated positive side of the power source.

wrong.0: The negative terminal is the opposite side and is marked with a minus sign.
wrong.1: The casing just holds the chemicals and does not indicate polarity.
wrong.2: This is the material inside and does not have a visible marking.

quiz.say: To make a battery work again, you must:
quiz.why: Recharging means pushing energy back into the chemical system.

wrong.0: Shaking will not restore the chemical reactants inside the battery.
wrong.1: Batteries need a specific electrical input to recharge properly.
wrong.3: Sunlight alone is not enough to reverse the chemical reaction.
